claim: Dorsal Excitor motor neuron DE-3 in the medicinal leech plays three very different dynamical roles in three different behaviors.
source: Dorsal Excitor motor neuron DE-3 in the medicinal leech plays three very different dynamical roles in three different behaviors.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a foundational premise of the study.

claim: Input synapses important for all the behaviors were widely distributed over DE-3's branches.
source: We found that input synapses important for all the behaviors were widely distributed over DE-3's branches, yet that functional clusters were different during (fictive) swimming vs. crawling.
evidence: This finding is directly stated in the abstract and supported by anatomical tracing data shown in the results.

claim: Functional clusters were different during (fictive) swimming vs. crawling.
source: We found that input synapses important for all the behaviors were widely distributed over DE-3's branches, yet that functional clusters were different during (fictive) swimming vs. crawling.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through clustering analysis in Figure 11.

claim: Barn owls use exquisitely tuned delay lines to locate sounds.
source: Examples include the exquisitely tuned delay lines that barn owls use to locate sounds (Carr and Konishi, 1988) and the motor neurons that control the honeybee's stinger (Ogawa et al., 1995).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Carr and Konishi, 1988).

claim: Motor neurons control the honeybee's stinger.
source: Examples include the exquisitely tuned delay lines that barn owls use to locate sounds (Carr and Konishi, 1988) and the motor neurons that control the honeybee's stinger (Ogawa et al., 1995).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Ogawa et al., 1995).

claim: Many circuits in most animals' central nervous systems respond to stimuli of multiple sensory modalities or control more than one behavior.
source: In most animals' central nervous systems, however, many circuits respond to stimuli of multiple sensory modalities or control more than one behavior (Briggman and Kristan, 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citation.

claim: Auditory stimuli can modulate activity in the human visual cortex in sighted as well as in blind subjects.
source: For instance, auditory stimuli can modulate activity in the human visual cortex (Plass et al., 2019) (in sighted as well as in blind subjects [Bedny et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Plass et al., 2019; Bedny et al., 2015).

claim: Motor cortex activity can be modulated by visual presentation of images of relevant body parts and in a working memory task in the absence of immediate stimuli.
source: Likewise, motor cortex activity can be modulated not just by visual presentation of images of relevant body parts, but even in a working memory task in the absence of immediate stimuli (Galvez-Pol et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Galvez-Pol et al., 2018).

claim: Multifunctionality may help smaller animals use their more constrained neural hardware more efficiently.
source: All these forms of multifunctionality likely contribute to the versatility of large brains like ours and may help smaller animals use their more constrained neural hardware more efficiently (Briggman and Kristan, 2008).
evidence: This is presented as a hypothesis supported by citation.

claim: In swimming, DE-3 oscillates at a relatively rapid 2 Hz in antiphase to its Ventral Excitor counterpart (VE-4).
source: In swimming, it oscillates at a relatively rapid 2 Hz in antiphase to its Ventral Excitor counterpart (VE-4) and controls the local dorsal flexion phase of the swim rhythm.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of DE-3 behavior during swimming.

claim: In crawling, DE-3 is active in phase with VE-4.
source: In crawling, it is active in phase with VE-4 and controls the contraction phase of the crawl rhythm.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of DE-3 behavior during crawling.

claim: In local bending, DE-3 operates in tight concert with its contralateral homolog as well as VE-4.
source: In 'local bending' it operates in tight concert with its contralateral homolog as well as VE-4 to precisely deform the local body wall away from a mechanical stimulus.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of DE-3 behavior during local bending.

claim: Calcium imaging has advanced to the point where simultaneous recordings from the vast majority of individual neurons in smaller species can be accomplished.
source: Activity imaging using calcium dyes has advanced to the point where simultaneous recordings from the vast majority of individual neurons in smaller species can be accomplished, for instance in larval zebrafish (Ahrens et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Ahrens et al., 2013).

claim: Calcium imaging has been applied to behaving animals.
source: This technique has even been applied to behaving animals (Jiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Jiao et al., 2018).

claim: Electron microscopy has advanced to the point that brains as large as that of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster can be imaged at synaptic resolution.
source: Likewise, anatomical imaging using electron microscopy (EM) has advanced to the point that brains as large as that of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster can be imaged—and substantial fractions of their circuitry reconstructed—at a synaptic resolution (Zheng et al., 2018; Bates et al., 2020; Scheffer et al., 2020; Maniates-Selvin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from multiple previous studies.

claim: Small vertebrate brains like that of larval zebrafish are yielding to electron microscopy approaches.
source: Even small vertebrate brains like that of larval zebrafish are yielding to this approach (Hildebrand et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Hildebrand et al., 2017).

claim: All nervous systems, even the simplest ones, exhibit considerable variability in their connectomes.
source: However, cross-identification of neurons between EM and functional imaging in this approach is ultimately limited by the fact that all nervous systems, even the simplest ones, exhibit considerable variability in their connectomes (Bhattacharya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Bhattacharya et al., 2019).

claim: Robustly linking function to connectivity requires a combined anatomical and functional assessment within the same animal.
source: Accordingly, robustly linking function to connectivity requires a combined anatomical and functional assessment within the same animal (Bargmann and Marder, 2013).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Bargmann and Marder, 2013).

claim: Two-photon calcium imaging in the mouse visual cortex followed by serial transmission electron microscopy of that same cortex was described in Nature.
source: Nearly a decade ago, back-to-back papers in Nature described two-photon calcium imaging in the mouse visual cortex followed by serial transmission electron microscopy of a small volume of that same cortex (Bock et al., 2011) and two-photon calcium imaging in the mouse retina followed by serial block face electron microscopy of that same retina (Briggman et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Bock et al., 2011; Briggman et al., 2011).

claim: CLEM has allowed the quantification of synaptic connections between functionally identified neurons that control eye movement in the larval zebrafish.
source: This approach, 'Correlated Light and Electron Microscopy' or CLEM (de Boer et al., 2015), has since allowed the quantification of synaptic connections between functionally identified neurons that control eye movement in the larval zebrafish (Vishwanathan et al., 2017), a reconstruction of the connections in the olfactory bulb of another larval zebrafish in which neural responses to eight different odors had been recorded prior to sectioning (Wanner and Friedrich, 2020), and a critical re-assessment of the mechanisms of selectivity to particular sensory features in neurons of the mammalian visual cortex (Scholl et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Vishwanathan et al., 2017).

claim: Voltage-sensitive dyes can capture faster temporal dynamics than calcium dyes.
source: For the present study of multifunctional behavioral circuits, we chose to use a voltage-sensitive dye (VSD) (Grinvald and Hildesheim, 2004; Kulkarni and Miller, 2017) rather than a calcium dye because it can capture faster temporal dynamics, potentially even recording individual action potentials, as well as both excitatory and inhibitory synaptic potentials.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the methodological choice and supported by citations.

claim: Voltage-sensitive dyes can record both excitatory and inhibitory synaptic potentials.
source: For the present study of multifunctional behavioral circuits, we chose to use a voltage-sensitive dye (VSD) (Grinvald and Hildesheim, 2004; Kulkarni and Miller, 2017) rather than a calcium dye because it can capture faster temporal dynamics, potentially even recording individual action potentials, as well as both excitatory and inhibitory synaptic potentials.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the methodological choice and supported by citations.

claim: This is the first time VSDs and SBEM have been combined at this scale.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first time VSDs and SBEM have been combined at this scale.
evidence: This is stated as a claim of novelty by the authors.

claim: The nervous system of the leech comprises cephalic ganglia, a tail ganglion, and 21 nearly identical segmental ganglia connected by a ventral nerve cord.
source: The nervous system of the leech comprises cephalic ganglia, a tail ganglion, and 21 nearly identical segmental ganglia connected by a ventral nerve cord (Muller et al., 1981; Wagenaar, 2015).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Muller et al., 1981; Wagenaar, 2015).

claim: Each leech ganglion consists of about 400 neurons.
source: Each ganglion consists of about 400 neurons (Macagno, 1980) with cell bodies arranged in a spherical monolayer around a central neuropil.
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Macagno, 1980).

claim: In the leech neuropil, neurons communicate through chemical and electrical synapses located along extensively branched neurites.
source: In the neuropil, neurons communicate through chemical and electrical synapses located along extensively branched neurites (Muller and McMahan, 1976; Fan et al., 2005; Pipkin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Muller and McMahan, 1976; Fan et al., 2005; Pipkin et al., 2016).

claim: The leech robustly expresses several behaviors even in reduced preparations.
source: The leech is an ideal model organism for this type of work, because it robustly expresses several behaviors even in reduced preparations (Kristan et al., 2005), its neurons are uncommonly accessible to physiological recording, and its cell bodies are relatively large and thus yield strong VSD signals (Briggman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Kristan et al., 2005).

claim: Leech neurons are uncommonly accessible to physiological recording.
source: The leech is an ideal model organism for this type of work, because it robustly expresses several behaviors even in reduced preparations (Kristan et al., 2005), its neurons are uncommonly accessible to physiological recording, and its cell bodies are relatively large and thus yield strong VSD signals (Briggman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Leech cell bodies are relatively large and thus yield strong VSD signals.
source: The leech is an ideal model organism for this type of work, because it robustly expresses several behaviors even in reduced preparations (Kristan et al., 2005), its neurons are uncommonly accessible to physiological recording, and its cell bodies are relatively large and thus yield strong VSD signals (Briggman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Briggman et al., 2005).

claim: An individual segmental ganglion is a good stand-in for a whole nervous system because its neurons capture the entire pathway from sensory input through self-generated interneuronal rhythms to motor output.
source: Crucially, an individual segmental ganglion is a good stand-in for a whole nervous system, because its neurons capture the entire pathway from sensory input through self-generated interneuronal rhythms to motor output (Kristan et al., 2005), which is why we focused our imaging efforts there.
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Kristan et al., 2005).

claim: 250 neurons were recorded simultaneously using VSD imaging.
source: We were able to record from 250 neurons simultaneously, similar to our previous results.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the VSD imaging experiment.

claim: Fictive swimming was induced by electrical stimulation of a posterior segment.
source: Fictive swimming was induced by electrical stimulation of a posterior segment, which resulted in characteristic rhythmic activity in dorsal motor neurons and many other neurons on both sides of the ganglion (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail and result.

claim: Electrical stimulation of a posterior segment resulted in characteristic rhythmic activity in dorsal motor neurons and many other neurons on both sides of the ganglion.
source: Fictive swimming was induced by electrical stimulation of a posterior segment, which resulted in characteristic rhythmic activity in dorsal motor neurons and many other neurons on both sides of the ganglion (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Coherence analysis confirmed that the rhythms of the various neurons were indeed related to the fictive behavior.
source: Coherence analysis confirmed that the rhythms of the various neurons were indeed related to the fictive behavior (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2c,d.

claim: The ganglion was fixated and embedded in a resin at the end of the behavior experiment.
source: At the end of the (fictive) behavior experiment, the ganglion was fixated and embedded in a resin.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological step.

claim: X-ray tomography was used to re-image the ganglion and verify that the cell bodies seen in the VSD images could still be identified.
source: To correlate light and electron microscopy, we then re-imaged the ganglion using X-ray tomography (Bushong et al., 2015) and verified that the cell bodies seen in the VSD images could still be identified (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The X-ray image stack was used to trace neuronal processes from the somata to the edge of the neuropil.
source: The X-ray image stack was also used to trace neuronal processes from the somata to the edge of the neuropil (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Serial blockface electron microscopy was chosen over serial-section transmission EM because SBEM can reliably process large numbers of slices with much lower risk of sectioning artifacts.
source: We chose serial blockface electron microscopy (SBEM) over serial-section transmission EM (Harris et al., 2006) because SBEM can reliably process large numbers of slices with much lower risk of sectioning artifacts.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the methodological choice.

claim: 78,803 images from 9604 slices were acquired, totaling 22.8 terapixels.
source: We acquired 78,803 images from 9604 slices, totaling 22.8 terapixels.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the SBEM imaging.

claim: The combined path length of the entire arborization of DE-3R was 6,109 μm.
source: The combined path length of the entire arborization of DE-3R was 6,109 μm (Figure 6a,b; Figure 7a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in the figures.

claim: 531 synapses onto DE-3R were identified.
source: We identified 531 synapses onto DE-3R.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the tracing analysis.

claim: 44 synapses onto DE-3R were formed by cells with somata in neighboring ganglia that were not included in the EM volume.
source: Of these, 44 were formed by cells with somata in neighboring ganglia that were not included in our EM volume (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in the figure supplement.

claim: 387 synapses onto DE-3R could be traced to their somata with a high degree of confidence.
source: Of the rest, 387 could be traced to their somata with a high degree of confidence.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the tracing analysis.

claim: 51 presynaptic neurons formed at least two synapses onto DE-3R.
source: To avoid false positives, we only considered presynaptic neurons that formed at least two synapses onto DE-3R. There were 51 of those.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the tracing analysis with a methodological criterion.

claim: 35 presynaptic neurons could be confidently matched to cell bodies seen in the VSD record.
source: Of those, 35 could be confidently matched to cell bodies seen in the VSD record, and of those, 10 could be confidently matched to specific identified neurons on the canonical map with previously described functions (Figure 7b and Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the cross-identification analysis.

claim: 10 presynaptic neurons could be confidently matched to specific identified neurons on the canonical map with previously described functions.
source: Of those, 35 could be confidently matched to cell bodies seen in the VSD record, and of those, 10 could be confidently matched to specific identified neurons on the canonical map with previously described functions (Figure 7b and Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the cross-identification analysis and shown in Figure 7b and Table 1.

claim: The average correlation between synapse count and coherence magnitude across eight trials was 0.16 ± 0.12.
source: On average across the eight trials in our data set, this correlation was 0.16 ± 0.12 (mean ± SD; t = 3.41; p = 0.011; two-tailed t-test), even though none of the individual correlation coefficients was statistically significant (Figure 9).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the correlation analysis and shown in Figure 9.

claim: The spatial distributions of excitatory and inhibitory synapses were not found to be different from the other ('unknown') synapses when distance was measured to the soma.
source: The spatial distributions of excitatory and inhibitory synapses were not found to be different from the other ('unknown') synapses, either when distance was measured to the soma (Figure 10b), or when it was measured to the primary neurite (Figure 10—figure supplement 1a) of the postsynaptic tree.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the spatial distribution analysis and shown in the figures.

claim: Cells associated with a specific behavior did not form synapses in specific locations at the macroscopic scale.
source: We asked whether cells associated in that way with a specific behavior would form synapses in specific locations, but found that was not the case at the macroscopic scale (Figure 10c,d and Figure 10—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the spatial analysis and shown in the figures.

claim: Spatial clustering of synapses of synchronized cell assemblies has been previously observed in other model organisms.
source: Such spatial clustering of synapses of synchronized cell assemblies has been previously observed in other model organisms (Takahashi et al., 2012; Varga et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Takahashi et al., 2012; Varga et al., 2011).

claim: Neighboring synapses that are less than 12–16 μm apart are more likely to be synchronized than synapses farther apart.
source: Findings from in vivo and in vitro studies have shown that neighboring synapses that are less than 12–16 μm apart are more likely to be synchronized than synapses farther apart (Kleindienst et al., 2011; Winnubst et al., 2015) and that local synaptic plasticity mechanisms act on similar spatial scales (5–10 µm; Harvey and Svoboda, 2007).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Kleindienst et al., 2011; Winnubst et al., 2015).

claim: Local synaptic plasticity mechanisms act on spatial scales of 5–10 µm.
source: Findings from in vivo and in vitro studies have shown that neighboring synapses that are less than 12–16 μm apart are more likely to be synchronized than synapses farther apart (Kleindienst et al., 2011; Winnubst et al., 2015) and that local synaptic plasticity mechanisms act on similar spatial scales (5–10 µm; Harvey and Svoboda, 2007).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Harvey and Svoboda, 2007).

claim: Parameter ranges could be identified for which spatial clusters corresponded to functional groupings in all but one trial.
source: In all but one trial, parameter ranges could be identified for which spatial clusters indeed corresponded to functional groupings (Figure 11b).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the clustering analysis and shown in Figure 11b.

claim: In the two swim trials, the peaks were located at dext = 61 ± 2 μm and 65 ± 2 μm respectively.
source: In the two swim trials, the peaks were located at dext = 61 ± 2 μm and 65 ± 2 μm respectively; in the two crawl trials at 14 ± 15 μm and 18 ± 3 μm.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the clustering analysis.

claim: In the two crawl trials, the peaks were located at dext = 14 ± 15 μm and 18 ± 3 μm.
source: In the two swim trials, the peaks were located at dext = 61 ± 2 μm and 65 ± 2 μm respectively; in the two crawl trials at 14 ± 15 μm and 18 ± 3 μm.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the clustering analysis.

claim: Functionally relevant spatial clusters during swimming were governed by very different parameter values than during crawling.
source: In summary, functionally relevant spatial clusters during swimming were governed by very different parameter values than during crawling.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion from the clustering analysis.

claim: The reconstructed morphology of DE-3R was in accordance with previous light microscopic studies in adult and electron microscopy in a juvenile ganglion.
source: The reconstructed morphology of DE-3R was in accordance with previous light microscopic studies in adult (Norris and Calabrese, 1987; Fan et al., 2005) and electron microscopy in a juvenile ganglion (Pipkin et al., 2016): its primary neurite emerged from the soma laterally and traveled toward the ipsilateral roots before making a 180° turn to run laterally across the ganglion.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with previous literature (Norris and Calabrese, 1987; Fan et al., 2005; Pipkin et al., 2016).

claim: The number of synapses onto DE-3R (531) was in the same range as the numbers previously reported for a juvenile ganglion (437 and 650).
source: Our tracing revealed 531 synapses onto DE-3R. This was in the same range as the numbers previously reported for a juvenile ganglion (437 and 650) (Pipkin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with previous literature (Pipkin et al., 2016).

claim: No output synapses from DE-3R onto other cells in the ganglion were found.
source: Unlike Pipkin et al., 2016, we did not find any output synapses from DE-3R onto other cells in the ganglion.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the tracing analysis and a comparison with previous literature.

claim: SBEM does not yet allow for the identification of gap junctions.
source: We focused here on chemical synaptic connections, since SBEM does not yet allow for the identification of gap junctions.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the SBEM method.

claim: Electrical synapses between DE-3R and their contralateral homologs as well as some interneurons do exist.
source: However, electrical synapses between DE-3R and their contralateral homologs as well as some interneurons do exist (Fan et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Fan et al., 2005).

claim: 21 neurons (including bilateral homologues) were previously found to be monosynaptically connected to the DE-3R motor neuron.
source: In previous reports, 21 neurons (including bilateral homologues) were found to be monosynaptically connected to the DE-3R motor neuron (Figure 12).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of previous literature and shown in Figure 12.

claim: Four previously reported presynaptic partners (bilateral DI-1, 107, and L) were matched to the presynaptic partners seen in the VSD imaging and identified with sufficient confidence.
source: Of those, four (bilateral DI-1, 107, and L) were matched to the presynaptic partners seen in the VSD imaging and identified with sufficient confidence.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the cross-identification analysis.

claim: Six other new partners were confidently identified (VI-2, 8, 101, 102, 109, and 117).
source: Six other new partners were confidently identified (VI-2, 8, 101, 102, 109, and 117), and a further 41 synaptic partners of DE-3R could not be confidently identified with any previously described neuron, mainly because our limited tracing did not allow a morphological identity match.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the cross-identification analysis.

claim: 41 synaptic partners of DE-3R could not be confidently identified with any previously described neuron, mainly because limited tracing did not allow a morphological identity match.
source: Six other new partners were confidently identified (VI-2, 8, 101, 102, 109, and 117), and a further 41 synaptic partners of DE-3R could not be confidently identified with any previously described neuron, mainly because our limited tracing did not allow a morphological identity match.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the cross-identification analysis with an explanation.

claim: The activity patterns observed during all three fictive behaviors exhibited by the single leech in this study matched observations from a larger group of animals reported before.
source: The activity patterns observed during all three fictive behaviors exhibited by the single leech in this study (Figures 2, 3 and 4) matched observations from a larger group of animals reported before (Tomina and Wagenaar, 2017): The majority of neurons in the ganglion were phasically active during multiple behaviors, indicating substantial but not complete overlap between the circuits that govern the behaviors (Briggman and Kristan, 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with previous literature (Tomina and Wagenaar, 2017; Briggman and Kristan, 2006).

claim: The majority of neurons in the ganglion were phasically active during multiple behaviors, indicating substantial but not complete overlap between the circuits that govern the behaviors.
source: The activity patterns observed during all three fictive behaviors exhibited by the single leech in this study (Figures 2, 3 and 4) matched observations from a larger group of animals reported before (Tomina and Wagenaar, 2017): The majority of neurons in the ganglion were phasically active during multiple behaviors, indicating substantial but not complete overlap between the circuits that govern the behaviors (Briggman and Kristan, 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a result and cited from previous literature (Briggman and Kristan, 2006).

claim: The leech used in this study was representative of its species.
source: There is considerable variation in the coherence values of specific cells between animals, but the data here fall within the range of values seen before. We conclude that the leech used in this study was representative of its species.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on comparison with previous data.

claim: No evidence of modular organization in DE-3R was found other than a slight trend that swim-associated synapses tended to be located closer to the primary neurite.
source: However, we found no evidence of such organization in DE-3R (Figure 10c,d) other than a slight trend that swim-associated synapses tended to be located closer to the primary neurite (Figure 10—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the spatial analysis and shown in the figures.

claim: The limited experimental evidence currently available suggests that even clusters of two synapses are functionally relevant in the mammalian cortex.
source: Indeed, the limited experimental evidence currently available suggests that even clusters of two synapses are functionally relevant in the mammalian cortex (Takahashi et al., 2012; Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Takahashi et al., 2012; Fu et al., 2012).

claim: Individual dendritic branches act as integrative compartments.
source: Findings from computational (Poirazi and Mel, 2001) and in vitro studies (Losonczy and Magee, 2006; Nevian et al., 2007) suggest that individual dendritic branches act as integrative compartments and that spatial synaptic clusters facilitate nonlinear dendritic integration.
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Poirazi and Mel, 2001; Losonczy and Magee, 2006; Nevian et al., 2007).

claim: Spatial synaptic clusters facilitate nonlinear dendritic integration.
source: Findings from computational (Poirazi and Mel, 2001) and in vitro studies (Losonczy and Magee, 2006; Nevian et al., 2007) suggest that individual dendritic branches act as integrative compartments and that spatial synaptic clusters facilitate nonlinear dendritic integration.
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Poirazi and Mel, 2001; Losonczy and Magee, 2006; Nevian et al., 2007).

claim: A set of parameter values was found for which synapses within spatial clusters also clustered in the phase space of the swim rhythm.
source: Indeed, we found a set of parameter values for which synapses within spatial clusters also clustered in the phase space of the swim rhythm and a different set of parameters for which synapses within spatial clusters also clustered in the phase space of the crawl rhythm (Figure 11b,c).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the clustering analysis and shown in Figure 11b,c.

claim: A different set of parameters was found for which synapses within spatial clusters also clustered in the phase space of the crawl rhythm.
source: Indeed, we found a set of parameter values for which synapses within spatial clusters also clustered in the phase space of the swim rhythm and a different set of parameters for which synapses within spatial clusters also clustered in the phase space of the crawl rhythm (Figure 11b,c).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the clustering analysis and shown in Figure 11b,c.

claim: Results were highly consistent between trials of the same behavior.
source: Results were highly consistent between trials of the same behavior.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the clustering analysis results.

claim: The results of clustering were not consistent among local bending trials.
source: (The results of clustering were not consistent among local bending trials. This may stem from a nature of this reflex behavior: the responsiveness of the population of neurons involving pressure sensation is variable, reflecting the plasticity of the circuit (Crisp and Burrell, 2009).)
evidence: This is stated as a result with a speculative explanation cited from previous literature (Crisp and Burrell, 2009).

claim: The responsiveness of the population of neurons involving pressure sensation is variable, reflecting the plasticity of the circuit.
source: (The results of clustering were not consistent among local bending trials. This may stem from a nature of this reflex behavior: the responsiveness of the population of neurons involving pressure sensation is variable, reflecting the plasticity of the circuit (Crisp and Burrell, 2009).)
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Crisp and Burrell, 2009) as an explanation.

claim: The strongest correspondence between spatial clusters and activity patterns was observed when synaptic clusters were defined by a maximum distance between nearest neighbors (dNN) of up to 10 µm.
source: In agreement with earlier reports (Kleindienst et al., 2011), the strongest correspondence between spatial clusters and activity patterns was observed when synaptic clusters were defined by a maximum distance between nearest neighbors (dNN) of up to 10 µm.
evidence: This is stated as a result and cited from previous literature (Kleindienst et al., 2011).

claim: Computational and in vitro studies indicate that 10–20 synchronized inputs are required to trigger dendritic spikes.
source: Computational and in vitro studies indicate that 10–20 synchronized inputs are required to trigger dendritic spikes (Ujfalussy and Makara, 2020).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Ujfalussy and Makara, 2020).

claim: Existing in vivo studies have found synchrony in only up to five neighboring dendritic spines.
source: Existing in vivo studies, however, have found synchrony in only up to five neighboring dendritic spines, making it unclear what the impact of the synaptic clusters on the membrane potential of the posysynaptic neuron might be.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of previous in vivo studies.

claim: Clusters of up to 23 synaptic members can display synchronous activity.
source: Indeed, our results indicate that clusters of up to 23 synaptic members can display synchronous activity.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the clustering analysis.

claim: Leech neurons have a unipolar morphology with the somata strictly segregated from neuropil.
source: Leech neurons—along with most neurons in the central nervous systems of other annelids, arthopods, and molluscs—have a unipolar morphology with the somata strictly segregated from neuropil (Bullock and Horridge, 1965).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Bullock and Horridge, 1965).

claim: With notable exceptions, leech somata are thought to play a relatively minor role in the integration of synaptic inputs to action potential outputs.
source: With notable exceptions (including sensory neurons in the leech and select insect motorneurons [Hancox and Pitman, 1992]), these somata are thought to play a relatively minor role in the integration of synaptic inputs to action potential outputs (Andjelic and Torre, 2005).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature (Hancox and Pitman, 1992; Andjelic and Torre, 2005).

claim: The completeness of the functional dataset in combination with anatomical data makes for an attractive basis for simulation studies to arrive at a computational understanding of multifunctional neuronal circuits.
source: Even so, the completeness of our functional dataset in combination with our anatomical data makes for an attractive basis for simulation studies to arrive at a computational understanding of multifunctional neuronal circuits (Real et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a potential application and cited from previous literature (Real et al., 2017).

claim: The data may serve as a large-scale ground truth for EM segmentation algorithms.
source: Our data may also serve as a large-scale ground truth for EM segmentation algorithms (Plaza and Funke, 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a potential application and cited from previous literature (Plaza and Funke, 2018).

claim: This study represents an important step in a combined approach to studying multifunctional circuits at the synaptic level.
source: This study not only represents an important step in a combined approach to studying multifunctional circuits at the synaptic level, but also lays the groundwork for a comprehensive neuronal mapping of a whole ganglion that semi-autonomously processes local sensory information and controls segmental movement.
evidence: This is stated as a summary claim by the authors.

claim: This study lays the groundwork for a comprehensive neuronal mapping of a whole ganglion that semi-autonomously processes local sensory information and controls segmental movement.
source: This study not only represents an important step in a combined approach to studying multifunctional circuits at the synaptic level, but also lays the groundwork for a comprehensive neuronal mapping of a whole ganglion that semi-autonomously processes local sensory information and controls segmental movement.
evidence: This is stated as a summary claim by the authors.

claim: The combination of anatomical methods with synaptic resolution and imaging techniques that can record from the entirety of the neurons of a circuit promises an extraordinary opportunity to assess neural computations at the level of circuit dynamics.
source: The combination of anatomical methods with synaptic resolution and imaging techniques that can record from the entirety of the neurons of a circuit promises an extraordinary opportunity to assess neural computations at the level of circuit dynamics.
evidence: This is stated as a forward-looking claim by the authors.

claim: Functional maps from recorded activity combined with anatomical connectomes are poised to become a powerful tool to have a better understanding of complex behaviors and to predict the outcomes of new manipulations.
source: Functional maps (Alivisatos et al., 2012) from recorded activity combined with anatomical connectomes (Denk et al., 2012; Bargmann and Marder, 2013; Morgan and Lichtman, 2013) are therefore poised to become a powerful tool not only to have a better understanding of complex behaviors, but also to predict the outcomes of new manipulations Devor et al., 2013; Kandel et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2013.
evidence: This is stated as a forward-looking claim and supported by multiple citations.

claim: This new addition with the annelid species to the developing field would pave the way for comparative approaches by functional connectomics to study evolutionary aspects of neuronal design.
source: This new addition with the annelid species to the developing field would also pave the way for comparative approaches by functional connectomics to study evolutionary aspects of neuronal design (Laurent, 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a forward-looking claim and cited from previous literature (Laurent, 2020).

claim: The spectral power in the images exceeded the noise floor set by shot noise at spatial frequencies up to about 20 lines/μm.
source: The spectral power in our images exceeded the noise floor set by shot noise at spatial frequencies up to about 20 lines/μm (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), corresponding to an effective pixel size of about 25 nm.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the image quality analysis and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The effective pixel size of the SBEM images was about 25 nm.
source: The spectral power in our images exceeded the noise floor set by shot noise at spatial frequencies up to about 20 lines/μm (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), corresponding to an effective pixel size of about 25 nm.
evidence: This is stated as a result derived from the spectral analysis.

claim: Synaptic vesicles appear merely as gray granules in the SBEM images because of limited resolution.
source: Because of limited resolution in our SBEM images, synaptic vesicles appear merely as gray granules (Figure 6c,d), but fields of such granules were clearly distinct from other gray areas in the SBEM images.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and shown in Figure 6c,d.

claim: Fields of granules were clearly distinct from other gray areas in the SBEM images.
source: Because of limited resolution in our SBEM images, synaptic vesicles appear merely as gray granules (Figure 6c,d), but fields of such granules were clearly distinct from other gray areas in the SBEM images.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and shown in Figure 6c,d.

claim: Comparison with digitally blurred TEM images confirmed the interpretation of granular areas as vesicles.
source: Comparison with digitally blurred TEM images (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) confirmed this interpretation.
evidence: This is stated as a validation and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Granular areas were concentrated in fiber endings and varicosities.
source: We found that granular areas were concentrated in fiber endings and varicosities.
